Okay, so I've been doing my best to consolidate my debt and pay off everything I accumulated since my early 20s. I admit fault in being reckless in the past financially but I am making an effort to right my wrongs. However, it has come to a point where I'm having to choose between paying rent and my car and having groceries or not eating and incurring more debt to try and get by. I currently owe around $16k in debt between Prosper and Lending Club. My question(s) is:

What could happen to me, legally, if I stopped paying those debts so I can keep a roof over my head and a car to drive to keep my job?

Can these companies sue? Garnish my wages? Will they be likely to settle on a lower amount? If my debt goes to collections how badly will this affect my credit score? Is there anything I haven't thought of that I should be looking at?

Please help.
NA - Questions about letting debt go to collections

If you stop paying, your credit score will drop like a rock, which will severely limit your access to credit, apartment rentals, good jobs (they run credit checks), etc.

After you stop paying, they will sue you, they will win, then they will garnish your wages. If you're lucky they might then offer to settle for less, but that will still involve you coming up with a large portion of the debt in cash (even if they settle for 1/3 that's still +$5k in cash you dont have).

So TLDR: Don't default on your debts. Do anything legal to avoid defaulting.

If you post a budget listing your monthly income and expenses, folks can usually provide advice on how to dig yourself out of this hole. $16k feels like a lot, but it's fixable.

Some companies may settle for a lower payment temporarily - like hardship. If the debt has already been sent to a collections agency, you may still negotiate with the original lender.

If I'm correct about Lending Club, the money lent to you is a private loan rather than a bank loan? Maybe you can talk to the lender about lowering your payments for 6 months, using financial hardship. You should probably look at the variable expenses and "wants" in your budget and try to minimize those as much as possible.

If you don't pay your debts, your credit will crash. It takes 7 years or more for a bad debt to fall off your credit - and it's 7 years after the last payment you made, not when you assumed the debt. Your wages may be garnished, but depending on the size of the debt (like the 16k is multiple $1k loans) that may not happen because it's not worth the cost to lender to sue for smaller debts.

If your debt goes into collections, you may negotiate with the collections agency. The original debt was written off as a loss by the lender and bought by the collection agency for pennies on the dollar. These agencies often add fees to raise the debt and try to collect all of it from you. If you negotiate, you have to be willing to make a payment right then and there - also, stick with what you can afford. Say you have $5000 that went into collections, and the agency is trying to get $6500 from you, but you can only possibly afford $3500. Tell them you can pay 1/3 right away and the rest within 6 months or something similar, and they may take the offer. If they don't take it, and you cannot afford anything else, you may just have to let it sit on your credit report for a while.

Personally, I've had some bad debt, and I've never had my wages garnished. I had a car loan I co-signed for go unpaid after 6 months, a landlord try to go after me for rent even though I broke the lease, some medical bills and small credit card debt I couldn't pay. This was my early 20's, and all of this went into collections. My credit score dropped to 420 or so, and I freaked out and asked my dad for advice. He used to work in repossession and finance, and told me all of this and some other advice. Some of the stuff they wouldn't negotiate, some companies did, some I proved they did something wrong in the process and the debt was off my back. Just don't assume any more debt until this is all taken care of.
